title: Coefficientwise map of polynomials and power series along a ring homomorphism
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $T$ an indeterminate. The *coefficientwise map* along $\varphi$ sends a polynomial $P=\sum_rc_rT^r\in R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] to $\varphi(P)=\sum_r\varphi(c_r)T^r\in S[T]$, and a formal power series $f=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in R[[T]]$ [def-weil-formal-power-series] to $\varphi(f)=\sum_{n\geq0}\varphi(c_n)T^n\in S[[T]]$; both maps are ring homomorphisms fixing $T$, and they agree on polynomials regarded as power series [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. For $R=\mathbf Z$, $S=\mathbf Q$ and $\varphi$ the inclusion $c\mapsto c\cdot1_{\mathbf Q}$, these are the inclusions $\mathbf Z[T]\subset\mathbf Q[T]$ and $\mathbf Z[[T]]\subset\mathbf Q[[T]]$, through which an integral polynomial or power series is regarded as a rational one.
